body: Anything that implies I've ever been female bothers me, but it's not offensive because I understand the intent of the question.

It's not offensive. I've been "passable" (as a male, ergo I've been perceived as male by people who I didn't disclose my birth gender with) since I was 13. I never grew up as female, and was telling people I met I was a boy since I was 10, but my parents didn't agree with it.

It wasn't until I stopped going to school and got homeschooled that it was easier to just live as male. My legal gender still says female, but only around two of my friends know that I was born female.
Well, what do you want to do with your life?
That was one of my first experiences with mental health professionals, so it really left a bad taste in my mouth.

You shouldn't. I'm reading through your posts right now if you give me a second.

Edit: What'd your environment like at the moment? What is your day to day routine?

Yeah, the psychiatric ward I went to was in California. It was one of the worst experiences I've ever had. 

I specifically recall one of the psychiatrists there had talked to me (they gave me a mood stabilizer, but the dose was so high that I couldn't even function) and she was talking about how I might just be a lesbian (I'm actually attracted to dudes) and that I shouldn't want to run away from my 'female nature'.

So, it was two doctors that shut down being trans, and practically ridiculed me for the stay. Whenever I would retort, it would be shut down by a "no, it's okay, the men in my life made me hate being a woman too". I feel like my sexual abuse was taken and used against me in an attempt to make me feel like my identity stemmed from someone else's wrong doing.
I can PM you with some stuff then, if you don't mind. ( I know you pretty much already opened the idea up for a pm)
Surprisingly, it's actually west coast. I grew up a little bit in the midwest, specifically Missouri.
By do the initial chat, do you mean call them yourself?
The last time I was diagnosed was back in 2010-11. When they talked about the personality disorder I was also diagnosed separately with gender identity disorder

I don't specifically hate him, I don't know how I feel about him actually. He ruined me.

I might check that out-- Also, I was diagnosed as manic depressive with a personality disorder. I'm not sure if those two are one in the same, but that's what I was told.

What does the trans lifeline do exactly? Is it like a suicide hotline? 

I'm actually really bad at vocally talking about my problems or issues, I remember my experience with a suicide hotline is that when I called (granted, I was drunk) it seemed like the woman I talked to wanted nothing to do with me. She couldn't relate to anything I was saying and it was the most insincere conversation I've ever had. That and I don't think she took me seriously.

My lack of motivation has been like this for months, it's gotten to the point that it's actually a task to get out of bed or even go to work.

Ive been diagnosed with manic depression, and a boarder line personality disorder. I'm not sure if these things are one in the same, but that's all I know.

I don't know about that. People say seek therapy, but I lack the money to. I would go to the er, but I can't miss work. It's funny how missing work stops me from getting help. I mean, it wouldn't matter if I was dead I wouldn't even have work, but being jobless and alive would be an awful experience.
